summary: This is a clean, attributable A/B. Each of the four m<=16 incumbents already uses the same grid, BLOCK_K, stage count and cp.async depth as the proposed swap-AB config, so tl.dot orientation (mma.sync+ldmatrix vs wgmma) is the only variable, and the 9 tests exercise the new path (m=1 qkv, m=7 pooler, m=5 unpooler slice). The archived evidence predicts flat for pooler and qkv_gate, with o at m=8 and the unpooler slice as the only real candidates, so judge it per shape on top_kernels, not on the headline.
justification: The mechanism is plausible in form: Triton gives tokens-on-M at BLOCK_M=16 mma.sync, and a 64-row weight tile on M with 16 tokens on N can lower to wgmma m64n16k16. Triton's MMAv3 rule (N%8==0, num_warps=4) allows that. But the evidence is weaker than the hypothesis claims, on three points. (1) The archived m<=16 incumbent diagnostics (pooler diag log) show n_regs=96, 0 spills, 120 KB smem, cp.async=90. Those are the same registers and bytes in flight as the swap-AB m=32 kernel (n_regs=96, cp.async=106, log 1602a4e947e64090). The 255-register pathology the m=32 win removed was the TMA variant only, and it does not exist at m<=16, as the Risk section itself concedes. (2) '+9.3% with the identical grid' was measured against SGLang's nvjet+splitKreduce at m=32 (21.97 -> 20.00 us shape time), not against the same-grid tokens-on-M Triton kernel at m<=16. (3) The cross-m kernel times from the same profiles predict flat. The swap-AB pooler ran 20.5 us of kernel at m=32 against the incumbent's 19.0/19.3/19.5 at m=1/8/16, and shape medians were 20.00 vs 19.85 at m=16. qkv_gate ran 12.1 us swap-AB at m=32 vs 11.8-12.3 incumbent. o ran 4.5 us vs 4.6/5.2/4.8. x bytes at m=32 are about 0.5 MB on a 67 MB stream, so halving tokens should change little. The pooler 'target <= 18 us' (3.7 TB/s) and the qkv/pooler 'faster' rows are therefore not supported; the most likely result is flat, within about 1 us of the incumbent. The only real candidates are o at m=8, whose 5.2 us is an outlier against 4.6 at m=1, and the unpooler slice. The slice is the furthest from its floor (4.5 us for 8.4 MB), but there the cost looks like fixed latency plus the 8-way split-K reduce rather than MMA issue, so wgmma may not help either. The expected directions agree with TASK.md: every changed shape is m in {1,8,16}, weight 62 in decode_1/decode_16/verify_1, and unpooler m=16 (full width, cuBLAS) and m>=17 are untouched. WEAKEST LINK: the assumption that the mma.sync+ldmatrix issue path, rather than HBM delivery at about 3.5 TB/s with 128 KB in flight per CTA, binds these streams at m<=16. The m=32 kernel times argue against it for the pooler and qkv_gate.
confounders: bf16-shape-gated-triton-winners-combo (658d63b): this is the incumbent being replaced on exactly these shapes (pooler/qkv_gate/o at m<=16, unpooler slice). It is the control, not a confounder. Its per-layer constants (grid, BLOCK_K, stages, SPLIT_K) are copied into SWAPAB16_CFG, so a difference in top_kernels times comes from the orientation/MMA path. If that combo had used other tiles, the comparison would mix tile and orientation effects; as written it does not.

bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton (8b9ad43): this supplies the kernel and is the evidence base. Shared-state risk only: the new path must use its own ws/cnt keys and its own WS_M=16. Master's _swapab_forward hardcodes WS_M=SWAPAB_MAX_M (32) and BLOCK_T=SWAPAB_BLOCK_T (32), and _swapab_route_ok requires 17<=m and w.shape==(n,k). If the build reuses those helpers unchanged, the [SPLIT_K,16,n] workspace gets addressed with a 32-row stride, which is an out-of-bounds/overlapping write and a correctness failure, and the unpooler slice (full 8192x4096 weight, n=1024) fails the shape check. These are not measurement confounders, but they must be parametrized.

sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity / router hypotheses: these cover a different layer or different shapes (m>=17 bf16 fallback, router), and the comparison is a paired ratio against SGLang in the same run. Not a confounder.
interference: No companion is warranted. (i) ab-revert of the shape-gated combo would compare swap-AB against cuBLAS, which the combo's own run already measured (5-17% Triton wins), so it adds nothing. (ii) ab-tune: the swap-AB config deliberately equals the incumbent's per layer, and tuning BLOCK_K or stages is a follow-up to a win, not something needed to read this result. (iii) control: the one sub-question, whether wgmma was actually emitted at n16 and at what register count, is answered by the prepare() PTX/regs print for both the new and the incumbent kernels in the same log. The shapes need no second run to read: Triton kernel times reproduce within about 1% (LESSONS), so per-shape top_kernels against the incumbent's archived times (pooler 19.0/19.3/19.5, qkv 11.8/12.0/12.3, o 4.6/5.2/4.8, unpooler slice 4.5/4.6 us) decide each layer independently. Faster rows go into a combo, slower rows revert to master's kernel. The headline will probably sit inside the ±1.5% CI and should not be the deciding signal. With bf16 checks spent and this going out as a scored submit, spending a second scored run on a companion is not justified.
rules_flags: None substantive. The weights are read in place as bf16 (the unpooler slice reads the first 1024 rows via stride_wn=4096, with no copy). fp32 accumulation and fp32 split-K partials match master's kernels. There is no autotune, nothing derived from inputs is cached, the routing branches only on cfg and shapes, and the diagnostic prints are in prepare() only. Keep report=False on the timed path.

Correctness hazard rather than rule: WS_M and BLOCK_T must be passed per path (16 for the new path), not taken from the m=32 module constants. Otherwise the 16-row workspace is overrun and the m=1 qkv, m=7 pooler and m=5 unpooler tests fail. A failure here costs a scored submit.
The ticket counters for the new path ([n//64] int32: pooler 64, qkv 36, unpooler slice 16) must be re-zeroed after the warm-ups, as the hypothesis says. o is SPLIT_K=1 and needs none.
open_questions: Does Triton emit wgmma for N=16 (m64n16k16) with the [BLOCK_K,16] K-major B tile, or fall back to mma.sync? The m=32 log only proves n32. If the PTX shows mma.sync, the run is a no-op that only says Triton will not reach wgmma at n16.

Unpooler slice: SPLIT_K=8 with K_SLICE=512 and BLOCK_K=128 is only 4 K-steps per CTA at 3 stages, so pipeline fill and the transposed fp32 reduce dominate. Will the wgmma path's prologue and the epilogue layout conversion through smem make it slower than the 4.5 us incumbent?

o at m=8 (5.2 us incumbent vs 4.6 at m=1) is the most likely real gain. Is that m=8 bump an incumbent artifact (for example BLOCK_M=16 masked load behaviour) that any non-M-specialized compile would remove? If so, attribute it to the compile, not to wgmma per se.

With do_not_specialize=['M'], m=1..16 share one compile per layer, but Triton still specializes stride_xm/stride_om by divisibility. Confirm the warm-up at m=1 and at m=16 hits the same cache entry, so the timed call never compiles.

If pooler and qkv_gate read flat or slower, as the m=32 kernel times predict, keep master's kernels for them in the follow-up combo and route only the layers that gained, with no rerun of identical code.
